review.why: Improves first-run onboarding and activation: aha moment, minimum path to value, checklists, empty states, stalled-user recovery and measurement.
review.summary: Defines a minimum path to value, then covers the first thirty seconds, checklists of three to seven items, empty states, guided tours and coordinated emails. It gives a cohort method for finding the aha moment that separates early actions from later retention, plus stalled-user recovery, a metrics list and an audit format.
strengths: Aha-moment method avoids common errors: immature cohorts and leaking the outcome into the predictor
Notes that correlation alone does not prove forcing an action causes retention
Ten-part toolkit with advice to use the fewest parts that reach value
cautions: Some figures, such as the checklist completion lift, are quoted without a source
Needs product analytics to find the aha moment
Activation models and path-to-value guides are in files not read here
